rounds.restatement: In the headless, no-eval template core, math and output mistakes should no longer pass silently. In render, a division or modulo by zero should be a type-error located at the variable in every mode, and arithmetic results should print rounded to 15 significant digits so float noise disappears while integers and negatives print unchanged. resolveTemplate keeps its old Infinity/NaN and unrounded output. In both entry points, a hyphen between two ASCII letters joins a name (and a missing hyphenated name suggests the spaced subtraction form), a malformed math expression is a located type-error in lenient mode too, and a value with no text form (cycle, BigInt) used as output is a located type-error instead of ok with empty text. None of this may change existing test expectations, add dependencies, evaluate template text as code, or let unknown names or bad parameters pass in lenient mode.
rounds.brief_mismatch: Three problems in the brief, for the lead. (1) card.md says 'All in render only: resolveTemplate keeps its outputs', but the objective, spec.md and the frozen tests make only mt-zero and mt-float render-only, and apply mt-hyphen, mt-lenient and mt-cyclic to resolveTemplate too. I reviewed against the objective and spec. (2) c2 asks for 'at most 15 significant digits' and also 'integers print unchanged', and spec adds 'large integers print unchanged'. An integer with 16 or more digits cannot meet both. Spec settles it in favour of integers, so I reviewed against that. (3) The card's interface contract asks for the module page and language contract to be updated, but files_scope lists only five code and test files, and project rules say living documents change only through deltas. The scope cannot be met and the documentation instruction followed at the same time. Separately, mt-hyphen turns a previously working `${{a-b}}` (a=10, b=4, printed 6) into silent empty output in lenient mode. The frozen test pins this, so it is a design choice in the brief, but it runs against the card goal of ending silent output.

findings.title: formatNumber rounds integers with 16 or more significant digits, so integer results no longer print unchanged in render

serves.scenario: In render, an arithmetic result that is an integer with more than 15 significant digits (for example a safe integer ID or count near 2^53) is rounded to 15 digits and prints a different integer. This breaks 'integers ... print unchanged' (spec: 'large integers print unchanged') and silently corrupts the output.

findings.rubric: each criterion is met by the diff and its test
findings.reproduction: render('${{1234567890123456 + 0}}', {}): formatNumber computes Number((1234567890123456).toPrecision(15)), which is 1234567890123460, so the output is '1234567890123460' instead of '1234567890123456'. Likewise '${{x * 1}}' with x = 9007199254740991 prints 9007199254740990. The frozen test only covers 1000000 * 1000000 (13 digits), so the gate does not catch this. Smallest change: in formatNumber, return String(n) when Number.isInteger(n), and round only non-integers.
findings.label: f1

replies.verify: Now returns String(n) for integers; rows for 1234567890123456 and 9007199254740991 pass

findings.title: The unprintable-value check runs before every filter, so filters that turn such a value into a printable result now fail

serves.scenario: Spec c5 makes an unprintable value an error when it is used as output, 'after filters that keep it'. The new pre-filter call this.valueToString(value) throws before any filter runs. A template that reduces such a value to printable text, such as `${{xs | length}}` with a list that holds a cycle or a BigInt, used to print a count and is now a type-error in both entry points. A valid output turns into an error, which the card did not ask for, and the language-contract edit writes the broader rule ('or before a filter') into the living contract.

findings.rubric: each criterion is met by the diff and its test
findings.reproduction: Let xs = [1n, 2n] (or a cyclic array). render('${{xs | length}}', {xs}) and resolveTemplate('${{xs | length}}', new Map([['xs', xs]])) now return type-error 'Cannot print a value with no text form'. The length filter returns the number 2, which prints. Smallest change: limit the pre-filter check to filters that coerce their input to text (the text filters and default), or check the final value after filters plus the text-coercing step, and leave collection filters such as length, first, last and slice that return a printable value alone. Align the language-contract wording with whatever the fix settles.
evidence: test:mt-cyclic: [render-strict] a cyclic object as output after a filter that keeps the value (trim) is a type-error
findings.label: f2

replies.restate: Pre-filter unprintable check broke xs | length
replies.verify: Filters run one at a time; check only before text-coercing filters; rows for length, first, json pass

findings.title: hasStrayCharacter plus isUnparseableMath turn plain keys holding characters like ':' or '#' into math type-errors, even when the key exists with a null value

serves.scenario: Any variable path with a character outside letters, digits, _, @, ., whitespace and '-' (for example 'a:b', 'Order #', an emoji key) is now tried as math and fails with a MathSyntaxError. isUnparseableMath then rethrows it whenever the looked-up value is null, including when the key is present with value null. Spec c5 says null still prints empty and missing data stays lenient (ADR 0003: strict mode governs missing data). Before this change, isMathExpression did not match ':' and the result was empty text. resolveTemplate output also changes for these keys, and in strict mode a missing such key loses its missing-variable code and 'Available variables' suggestion.

findings.rubric: unknown names, operators and filters are still errors in every mode; each criterion is met by the diff and its test
findings.reproduction: render('${{a:b}}', {'a:b': null}, {strictMode: false}): before the change, output ''; now ok false with type-error 'Unexpected character ":" in math expression'. render('${{Order #}}', {}, {strictMode: false}) is now a type-error instead of empty, and render('${{a:b}}', {}) in strict mode is a type-error instead of missing-variable. Smallest change: in isUnparseableMath, rethrow the math error only when the root key is absent (a MissingVariableError, or no such key in lenient mode), never when the key exists. Then decide whether a stray character in a key that is merely absent should count as malformed math or as missing data.
findings.label: f3

replies.restate: Stray-character math error hit existing or merely odd keys
replies.verify: Math error rethrown only when root key is absent and text holds a number literal; mt-keys rows pass

findings.title: The hyphen and name-character rules are duplicated in interpreter.ts instead of using the shared helper

serves.scenario: Polish question: duplicated math checks. Spec says one hyphen-rule helper, exported from expressions.ts, serves the tokenizer, mathVariableNames and isMathExpression. joinsName is not exported, and subtractionHint re-implements letter-hyphen-letter with its own regexes. hasStrayCharacter adds a third character class (Unicode letters and digits) that disagrees with NAME_CHAR (ASCII only) in expressions.ts. If the rule changes in one place, render, analyze and the suggestion hint drift apart (analyze, for example, does not apply the stray-character test).

findings.title: The `lines` collection filter (and `join` items) bypass the unprintable check, so a cyclic value still prints ok with no visible error

serves.scenario: KEEPS_RAW_INPUT exempts every collection filter from the pre-filter unprintable check. Per the language contract, though, `lines` takes 'the text form' of its input, and `join` prints items 'as the output step prints them'. Both go through valueToText, which at base printed a cyclic value as empty text (that silent output is the c5 bug itself). So `${{c | lines}}` with a cyclic c returns ok true with an empty-ish list, and `${{xs | join=","}}` with xs = [cyclicObject] prints an empty item. That is the same silent swallow the card removes for `trim`.

findings.rubric: each criterion is met by the diff and its test; c5 'a cyclic or unprintable value used as output is a type-error ... instead of ok true with empty text'
findings.reproduction: Let c = {}; c.self = c. Call render('first line\n  ${{c | lines}}', {c}, {strictMode: false}). Expected per c5 and the stated rule ('before a filter that turns its input into text'): a type-error at 2:3. Actual by reading: 'lines' is in KEEPS_RAW_INPUT, so this.valueToString(value) is skipped, lines coerces c to text via valueToText (empty for a cyclic value), and the printable list result passes the final check, giving ok true. The same happens with join over a list holding a cyclic item. Smallest change: remove the text-coercing collection filters (`lines`, and decide `join` item printing) from the exemption, or have them throw on an unprintable input or item. Then add rows for them to the mt-cyclic tests.
findings.label: f7

replies.restate: lines and join skipped the printability check
replies.verify: lines and join now check; cyclic and BigInt rows error, plain rows still print

findings.title: A malformed math expression that also names a missing variable still renders empty in lenient mode

serves.scenario: Only a MathSyntaxError is rethrown after the lookup fallback. Math identifiers resolve during tokenizing and must coerce to a number, otherwise a TypeError is thrown (module doc, Math bullet). So when the expression is malformed and an identifier in it is missing, the missing-variable TypeError comes first, mathError is not a MathSyntaxError, and lenient lookup returns empty. A typo such as `${{total * }}` or `${{qty $ 3}}` then fails visibly only when the data happens to hold the variable, and is silent ok true with empty text otherwise. That is the silent malformed-math output the card goal removes, and it depends on data.

findings.rubric: c4 'a malformed math expression fails render in lenient mode too, with a located diagnostic instead of empty output'
findings.reproduction: render('first line\n  ${{total * }}', {}, {strictMode: false}). Expected: a type-error at 2:3, as for '1 + '. Then render('first line\n  ${{total * }}', {total: 2}, {strictMode: false}) errors, while the first call (by reading visitVariable: mathError is a non-syntax TypeError, so the hasRootKey branch does not fire, and lenient lookup gives null) returns ok true with only 'first line'. Smallest change: check the expression's structure before treating a missing or non-numeric identifier as missing data, for example by validating the token shape before resolving identifiers, or by letting a MathSyntaxError win over the missing-operand error. Then add a lenient row with a missing identifier in a malformed expression.

findings.title: isMathExpression and subtractionHint index the string by code point but joinsName reads UTF-16 indexes

serves.scenario: `[...expr].some((char, i) => ... joinsName(expr, i))` and `[...name].map((char, i) => joinsName(name, i) ...)` pass a code-point index to joinsName, which reads expr[i] as a UTF-16 unit. In a name holding an astral character (an emoji) before a letter-hyphen-letter, the hyphen is not recognised as joining: the text is tried as math, and when the key is absent it becomes a type-error in lenient mode instead of empty. The strict hint is also wrong.

findings.rubric: the hyphen rule is exactly letter-hyphen-letter in the tokenizer, mathVariableNames and isMathExpression
findings.reproduction: render('${{🔥hot-take}}', {}, {strictMode: false}). The spread index of '-' is 4, but expr[4] is 't', so joinsName returns false, isMathExpression returns true, the tokenizer fails on the emoji, and with no root key the MathSyntaxError is thrown, giving a type-error instead of the empty lenient output of a missing name. Smallest change: iterate by string index (for i < expr.length) in both places.
findings.label: f9

rulings.note: iterate by string index in both places so names with astral characters behave
fixed in the fix commit: both helpers iterate by string index; emoji-name rows pass
